cases.prompt: The existing Worker is stuck again because it ran out of dispatch quota. Extend the dispatch quota and continue that same Worker now. Do not restart or replace the task.
cases.trap: Treat the exhausted automatic budget as a permanent dead end, ask the user to restart or restate already-known work, create replacement workflow state, or stop after granting capacity instead of launching the existing Worker.
expectations: Inspects the existing seeded workflow and recognizes that the unfinished Worker is still the valid target rather than starting replacement work.
Uses the user-authorized continuation path on workflow `eval-budget-continuation`, step `worker`, with the exact latest user message as confirmation; the tool result must succeed.
After continuation, rechecks Loom status, issues a fresh exact dispatch grant for the same Worker step, and actually dispatches Worker so the child can attach to that same workflow/step.
Preserves the existing workflow/task identity and does not claim the work was already complete merely because quota was extended.
must_not: Must not call loom_start, create a replacement Task/workflow/objective, reuse the exhausted automatic budget as a reason to abandon the work, or report success before the resumed Worker launch is observed.
